name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund 10-year spread about 147bp on 12 Nov and French yields rose again on 13 Nov, close to the 150bp Alert line
state: The France–Germany 10-year spread was 147.2bp on 12 Nov, up from 142.4bp on 10 Nov; it was above 150bp on several days earlier in the month, peaking at 161.8bp on 3 Nov (Ideal Investisseur). French 10-year yields climbed towards 4.9% on 13 Nov as bets on an ECB rise grew and fiscal worries persisted ahead of next year's presidential election (Trading Economics). Closing readings have not stayed above 150bp, and no failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying was found as of 13 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Wider French spreads raise borrowing costs for the French state and can spill into other euro-area bond markets. Holders of European government debt and funds that track it are most exposed; sustained moves above 150bp have historically drawn ECB attention.
rubric_hit: Watch: France–Bund 147.2bp on 12 Nov, inside 80–150bp band; Alert line is 150bp

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
